verses.text: When the day of Pentecost arrived, they were all together in one place.
Suddenly a sound like a powerful wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting.
They saw what looked like tongues of fire spreading out and resting on each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began speaking in other languages as the Spirit enabled them.
At that time, devout Jews from every nation under heaven were living in Jerusalem.
When they heard the sound, a crowd gathered, completely confused, because each person heard them speaking in their own language.
They were amazed and wondered, saying, “Aren’t all these people speaking Galileans?
“So how are we each hearing our own native language?
“We’re Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and people from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia,
“Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, and the parts of Libya near Cyrene. Some of us are visitors from Rome, both Jews and converts to Judaism;
“and some are Cretans and Arabs. Yet we hear them speaking in our own languages about the mighty works of God!”
They were all amazed and puzzled, asking one another, “What does this mean?”
Others made fun of them and said, “They’ve had too much new wine.”
Peter stood up with the eleven, raised his voice, and addressed them: “People of Judea and everyone living in Jerusalem, listen closely to what I’m telling you.
“These people aren’t drunk, as you think. It’s only nine in the morning!
“What you’re seeing is what the prophet Joel spoke about:
“‘God says: In the last days I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy; your young men will see visions, and your elders will dream dreams.
“‘In those days I will pour out my Spirit on my male and female servants, and they will prophesy.
“‘I will show wonders in the sky above and signs on the earth below: blood, fire, and clouds of smoke.
“‘The sun will turn dark and the moon red like blood before the Lord’s great and glorious day arrives.
“‘Everyone who calls on the Lord’s name will be saved.’
“People of Israel, listen to this: Jesus of Nazareth was a man God showed you was from him through powerful works, wonders, and signs—which God did among you, as you know.
“He was handed over according to God’s set plan and foreknowledge. You used lawless people to nail him to a cross and kill him.
“But God raised him up and freed him from death’s agony, because death couldn’t hold on to him.
“David said about him: ‘I always saw the Lord before me. He is at my right hand, so I won’t be shaken.
“‘That’s why my heart is glad and my words are full of joy. My body, too, will live in hope,
“‘because you will not abandon me to the grave or let your Holy One decay.
“‘You have shown me the paths of life; your presence fills me with joy.’
“Brothers and sisters, I can speak plainly about our ancestor David: he died, was buried, and his tomb is still here with us.
“He was a prophet and knew God had sworn to him that one of his descendants, in human lineage, would sit on his throne.
“David saw ahead and spoke about the Messiah’s resurrection: he would not be left among the dead, and his body would not decay.
“God raised this Jesus to life, and all of us are witnesses.
“Now exalted to God’s right hand, he received the promised Holy Spirit from the Father and has poured out what you now see and hear.
“David himself did not go up to heaven, but he says: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand
“‘“until I put your enemies under your feet.”’
“So all Israel should know for certain that God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.”
When the people heard this, it hit them hard. They asked Peter and the other apostles, “Brothers, what should we do?”
Peter told them, “Turn back to God, and each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. Then you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
“This promise is for you, your children, and everyone far away—for all whom the Lord our God calls to himself.”
With many other words Peter warned them and urged them, “Be saved from this corrupt generation!”
Those who gladly accepted his message were baptized. About three thousand people were added that day.
They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching, to fellowship, to sharing meals, and to prayer.
Everyone was filled with awe, and the apostles performed many wonders and signs.
All the believers stayed together and shared everything they had.
They sold their possessions and belongings and distributed the money to anyone who needed help.
Every day they met together at the temple. They shared meals in their homes with glad and sincere hearts.
They praised God and had the goodwill of all the people. And day by day the Lord added to their community those who were being saved.
